newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil house to vote civil service reforms today.
newsitem.headline: Brazil house to vote civil service reforms today.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies will vote on the outstanding and highly controversial amendments to the government's civil service reform bill Wednesday, even if it means a late-night session, the head of the lower house said.
Deputy Michel Temer, President of the Chamber of Deputies, told reporters the quorum was high.
"No one leaves today without voting," Temer said.
The civil service reforms, which aim to do away with salary privileges for public sector workers and to end lifetime job guarantees, were approved on the floor of the house in April.
But the government has since failed to muster the courage to force a vote on controversial amendments that threaten to make a mockery of the reforms by reestablishing so-called "job stability".
The lower house was due to begin its afternoon session at 1430 local time/1330 EDT/1730 GMT, with voting expected to begin two hours later, officials said.
The session runs till 2000 local time, but Temer said he would extend it indefinitely if balloting had not taken place by then.
